cards.explanation: The answer is fire. When Solomon, Israel's king, finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the burnt offering and the sacrifices. Nobody lit that one with a match, friends. I've watched my oven for years and it has never once done that on its own.
The answer is fills. The glory of the LORD filled the temple (2 Chronicles 7:1). That's the very moment the fire comes down and consumes the offerings. The very next verse shows how full it was.

The answer is False. The text says the priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled it. They couldn't go in, and that's the whole point of the verse. The glory of the LORD filled that house, friends.

The answer is that they bowed with their faces to the ground. All the Israelites saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple, and they bowed down on the pavement with their faces to the ground. Then they worshiped and gave thanks. Faces to the ground, friends, all of them.

The answer is dedicated. The king and all the people dedicated the house of God. Notice that it's the king AND all the people, not just one man with a crown. That's a whole crowd of hands in one batch.

The answer is King David. The text says the Levites had the musical instruments of the LORD, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD. It adds that David had offered praise with them, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.” Those words from David show up again in this very verse.

The answer is True. The priests sounded trumpets across from the Levites, and all the Israelites were standing. So the whole crowd is on its feet while the trumpets sound. That's a LOUD moment, friends.

The answer is that the bronze altar can't hold them all. The text says the bronze altar Solomon had made could not hold all these offerings. So he consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and offered them there. Too many offerings for the altar, so he used the courtyard.

The answer is False. The seven-day feast ends, but the text says that on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly. The dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days more. So there's still one more gathering before anyone leaves.

The answer is happy and full of joy. Solomon sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart. The text says it was for the good things that the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for His people Israel. They left with their hearts full, and I think that's the best way to leave any gathering.
